challenges.name: token-budget-context-packer
challenges.title: Write pack_context(chunks, budget, max_per_source)
challenges.description: Build the context block of the prompt from ranked chunks. Each used chunk becomes a line "[n] text", where n is the citation number of its source (numbered from 1 in order of first use). Keep the total count_tokens() cost of the lines within budget: skip a chunk that does not fit and keep going, use at most max_per_source chunks per source, and skip text already in the context. A skipped chunk never takes a citation number. Return the context, the cited sources in number order, the ids used and the token total.

challenges.name: prompt-budget-and-t-strings-quiz
challenges.title: Budgets and t-string templates
challenges.description: Check how the context budget is computed and what Python 3.14 template strings give you.

questions.question: The model has a 16,000-token context window. Which of these must be subtracted from it before you know how many tokens the retrieved chunks may use? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Everything the model reads or writes in one call shares the window: the system prompt, the user's question (and any conversation history you send), the formatting around the chunks, and the tokens the answer will need - if you do not reserve them, the API either rejects the request or cuts the answer short. The size of the index is irrelevant: only the chunks you actually put in the prompt count.

options.text: The user's question and the conversation history you send.
Tokens reserved for the model's answer.
The number of chunks stored in the vector index.

questions.question:
In Python 3.14, what is the value of prompt after

prompt = t"<context>
{context}
</context>
Question: {question}"
questions.explanation: A t-string (PEP 750) evaluates its expressions like an f-string, but does not join the result into a str. It returns a string.templatelib.Template: iterating it yields the static strings and Interpolation objects (value, expression, conversion, format_spec), and .interpolations lists the values. Code that renders the template decides how each value is inserted - for a prompt, for example, by neutralising a retrieved chunk that contains "</context>" so it cannot close the block early.

options.text: A str with context and question already substituted, like an f-string.
A string.templatelib.Template holding the static text and Interpolation objects, to be rendered by your own code.
A lazy f-string that is rendered the first time it is converted with str().
A SyntaxError: the t prefix is only valid for bytes literals.
